title: Basic SQL Training: Behind the Scenes of Foundational SQL Instruction at CU Friday Activities
image1Description: Serving as a technical staff member, providing guidance and assistance to activity participants

section1.heading: Origin and Intent
section1.content: During the 4th week of CU Friday Activities, centered on 'Basic SQL Training,' the primary goal was to open the door to the world of data for students starting from zero. My intention as a staff member was to be the 'first line of support,' helping participants overcome their fear of coding and ensuring they could successfully complete their first database tasks with confidence.

section2.heading: Role and Action
section2.content: I served as a Teaching Assistant (TA) and technical support staff. I actively engaged with participants during the workshop segments to explain basic command structures—Select, Insert, Update, and Delete—in an easy-to-understand manner. Additionally, I was responsible for on-site 'Debugging' when participants encountered syntax errors, helping them identify mistakes and teaching them how to interpret error messages so they could troubleshoot independently in the future.

section3.heading: Challenges
section3.content: The main challenge of this role was managing the diverse levels of technical understanding within a limited timeframe. I had to adapt my explanation methods to suit individual questions based on varying backgrounds and work against the clock to ensure everyone could execute their queries successfully according to the lesson plan, ensuring no one was left behind.

section4.heading: Results and Learning
section4.content: Most participants successfully completed the basic workshops and developed a positive attitude toward programming. This experience enhanced my 'Empathetic Mentoring' skills—teaching with an understanding of the learner's perspective. It also allowed me to solidify my own SQL fundamentals by answering a wide range of questions, providing a crucial foundation before I transitioned into a speaker role in subsequent sessions.
